introduction: These are working papers: letters from Bahá’u’lláh, his secretary and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá about orphans’ funds, promissory notes, receipts, partnerships that should or should not be entered, debts paid by friends, wills to be carried out to the letter, land bought and sold, money that did not arrive. The guide’s title names what they show: the people behind the accounts. The scriptures have such pages too. Jeremiah signs and seals a deed before witnesses; the Qur’an commands that debts be written by a scribe and that orphans’ wealth be kept apart; Paul travels with auditors and offers to pay a runaway’s debts; the first church appoints seven men to see that widows get their share. Three companions mark real tensions. Jesus would not divide an inheritance, and said no one can serve God and mammon. Polonius would keep friends and loans apart. And where Moses and the Qur’an forbid usury, reading 270 permits interest.
questions: Jesus refused to be “a judge or a divider” over an inheritance. What do these letters show about why a religious leader might take up such work, and how it can be done without becoming mammon’s servant?
The Qur’an requires that debts be written down. Why do readings 61 to 69 treat receipts and records as a moral matter and not only a practical one?
Polonius: “loan oft loses both itself and friend.” What practices in the readings protect friendships that money has entered?
Reading 270 permits interest, which Exodus and the Qur’an forbid. What reasons can be given for the change, and what in the older prohibition should a believer still honour?
“There is no wealth but life.” Pick three of the letters and say whose life each is protecting.

outside.why: Do not entrust orphans’ funds to a single person. The Qur’an: give unto orphans their wealth; nor absorb their wealth into your own wealth. Lo! that would be a great sin.
Why so much care over these accounts: a father of the fatherless, and a judge of the widows, is God in his holy habitation.
Father and son should consult each other in business. Where no counsel is, the people fall: but in the multitude of counsellors there is safety.
Money collected for one purpose must be used for it. Paul, handling a relief fund: providing for honest things, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men.
If ye have not been faithful in that which is another man’s, who shall give you that which is your own?
Strive to the utmost in business, and likewise in spreading the message. Not slothful in business; fervent in spirit; serving the Lord.
Jesus: no man can serve two masters; ye cannot serve God and mammon. The reading asks for the utmost effort in both business and faith. How is that not the divided service he rules out?
Business is difficult for those who are known in the Cause, since their conduct reflects on it. A good name is rather to be chosen than great riches.
Do not enter the company in person; sell the shares. Which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it?
Their well-being lies in ceasing “scattered and diverse trading ventures”. A faithful man shall abound with blessings: but he that maketh haste to be rich shall not be innocent.
The settlement of debts brings gladness. Owe no man any thing, but to love one another.
The former trade “is the cause of thy comfort”; a new one will absorb the mind. Study to be quiet, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands.
A promissory note, a seal, a named debtor. The Qur’an’s longest verse is on exactly this: when ye contract a debt for a fixed term, record it in writing; let a scribe record it between you in equity.
Whoever pays must obtain a receipt. Jeremiah buying a field: I subscribed the evidence, and sealed it, and took witnesses, and weighed him the money in the balances.
Record what was spent and what was lost, that the remainder be known. Give an account of thy stewardship.
A sale not established on a firm footing is set aside. Just balances, just weights, a just ephah, and a just hin, shall ye have.
They must keep accounts and collect, since they owe others and “payment of debts is necessary”. The wicked borroweth, and payeth not again: but the righteous sheweth mercy, and giveth.

Polonius would have his son out of the whole business: neither a borrower nor a lender be; for loan oft loses both itself and friend. These letters are full of loans between friends. What do they do to keep both the loan and the friend?
“What taketh precedence over all else today is unity, harmony and rendering unto each his due right.” First be reconciled to thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift.

Asked to make a brother divide an inheritance, Jesus refused: man, who made me a judge or a divider over you? and warned against covetousness. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá and his father did act as arbiters in such matters, patiently and in detail. Why would one teacher decline the role and another accept it?
Friends joined to pay off another’s debts. Paul of a runaway slave: if he hath wronged thee, or oweth thee ought, put that on mine account; I will repay it.
A loan to a friend in need is counted as service. He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the Lord.

A brother’s debt and how it was met. Elisha to the widow whose creditor was coming for her sons: go, borrow thee vessels abroad of all thy neighbours; and the oil stayed only when the vessels were full.
A caretaker may live there, but ownership stays where it is, and is recorded. Put the evidences in an earthen vessel, that they may continue many days.
He wrote his will with his own hand before he died. Isaiah to a sick king: set thine house in order.
Shares of an inheritance are assigned. The daughters of Zelophehad asked for a possession among their father’s brethren, and the answer was: they speak right.
Carry out the will exactly. A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children’s children.
Which comes first: the Right of God, the debts, or the funeral? Paul’s rule for ordering obligations: render therefore to all their dues: tribute to whom tribute is due; custom to whom custom.

Two newcomers said that what was allotted to them was not reaching them. In Jerusalem widows were being neglected in the daily ministration, and seven men of honest report were appointed over this business.
A sum is scraped together and sent. The disciples, every man according to his ability, determined to send relief.
Funds due to a member of the household are not to be delayed. At his day thou shalt give him his hire, neither shall the sun go down upon it; for he is poor, and setteth his heart upon it.
Land on Mount Carmel is given for a sacred purpose. Abraham insisted on paying full price for the field and the cave, and it was made sure unto him for a possession.
Money is assigned to build the graves of two honoured friends. Joseph of Arimathaea gave a new sepulchre in a garden.
May unproductive land be sold? In the morning sow thy seed, and in the evening withhold not thine hand: for thou knowest not whether shall prosper.
Property in ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s own name is to be registered and sold. Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth.
A group wishes to leave everything and come to the Holy Land, and is advised not to. Abraham went out, not knowing whither he went. When is leaving one’s livelihood faith, and when is it imprudence?

Interest on loans is declared lawful. The Qur’an: God permitteth trading and forbiddeth usury. Moses forbade it on loans to the poor, and Aristotle called money breeding money unnatural. The reading reverses a prohibition three thousand years old. On what grounds, and with what limits?
If thou lend money to any of my people that is poor by thee, thou shalt not be to him as an usurer. The older law protects the poor borrower. What protects him under the new permission?
Profit in cash transactions is permitted within fairness. A false balance is abomination to the Lord: but a just weight is his delight.
The Right of God is reckoned on what remains of income after the year’s expenses. Bring ye all the tithes into the storehouse.

What is found on the road must be restored if its owner can be found. Thou shalt not see thy brother’s ox or his sheep go astray, and hide thyself from them: thou shalt in any case bring them again unto thy brother.
The guide’s arc ends with the people behind the accounts. Ruskin: there is no wealth but life.

shortfall: Most of these hundred readings are instructions about particular debts, properties, shipments and persons, intelligible only in their circumstances; companions were given where a principle shows (trust funds, written records, consultation, paying debts, wills, relief, lawful interest) and not otherwise.

philemon-put-that-on-mine-account.text: If he hath wronged thee, or oweth thee ought, put that on mine account; I Paul have written it with mine own hand, I will repay it

deuteronomy-bring-them-again-unto-thy-br.text: Thou shalt not see thy brother's ox or his sheep go astray, and hide thyself from them: thou shalt in any case bring them again unto thy brother

exodus-neither-lay-upon-him-usury.text: If thou lend money to any of my people that is poor by thee, thou shalt not be to him as an usurer, neither shalt thou lay upon him usury

proverbs-inheritance-to-his-childrens-ch.text: A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children's children: and the wealth of the sinner is laid up for the just

quran-trade-permitted-usury-forbidden.text: Those who swallow usury cannot rise up save as he ariseth whom the devil hath prostrated by (his) touch. That is because they say: Trade is just like usury; whereas Allah permitteth trading and forbiddeth usury

quran-record-it-in-writing.text: O ye who believe! When ye contract a debt for a fixed term, record it in writing. Let a scribe record it in writing between you in (terms of) equity

quran-wealth-of-orphans.text: Give unto orphans their wealth. Exchange not the good for the bad (in your management thereof) nor absorb their wealth into your own wealth. Lo! that would be a great sin.

shakespeare-neither-a-borrower.text: Neither a borrower nor a lender be; / For loan oft loses both itself and friend, / And borrowing dulls the edge of husbandry.
shakespeare-neither-a-borrower.author: William Shakespeare
